title: Thermal Management
description: Optimize your HP OMEN's cooling system for better performance and longevity. Learn to monitor temperatures, configure fan profiles, and improve thermals.

steps.title: OMEN Thermal Profiles
steps.content:
OMEN Command Center offers three thermal profiles for different use cases:

**❄️ Cool Mode**
• Fan Behavior: Quiet operation, lower fan speeds
• Performance: 70-80% of max
• Temps: 60-75°C under load
• Best For: Office work, web browsing, quiet environments

**⚖️ Default Mode**
• Fan Behavior: Balanced fan curves
• Performance: 85-90% of max
• Temps: 70-85°C under load
• Best For: General use, light gaming

**🔥 Performance Mode**
• Fan Behavior: Aggressive cooling, higher fan speeds
• Performance: 100% max
• Temps: 80-95°C under load
• Best For: Gaming, rendering, heavy workloads

infoBox.title: Quick Switch
infoBox.content: Use the keyboard shortcut Fn + P to quickly cycle through thermal profiles without opening OMEN Command Center.

steps.title: Temperature Guidelines
steps.content:
Monitor your temperatures to ensure your system stays healthy:

**CPU Idle:** Safe: 35-50°C | Warning: 50-60°C | Danger: 60°C+

**CPU Gaming:** Safe: 70-85°C | Warning: 85-95°C | Danger: 95°C+

**GPU Idle:** Safe: 30-45°C | Warning: 45-55°C | Danger: 55°C+

**GPU Gaming:** Safe: 65-80°C | Warning: 80-90°C | Danger: 90°C+

**SSD:** Safe: 30-50°C | Warning: 50-70°C | Danger: 70°C+

infoBox.title: Throttling Warning
infoBox.content: If your CPU consistently hits 95°C+, it will thermal throttle, reducing performance. Consider improving cooling or undervolting.

steps.title: Monitoring Tools
steps.content:
Use these tools to monitor your system temperatures:

**OMEN Command Center** (Pre-installed)
Built-in HP monitoring with thermal controls. Features: Real-time temps, Fan control, Performance profiles

**HWiNFO64** (https://www.hwinfo.com/)
Comprehensive hardware monitoring. Features: Detailed sensors, Logging, Alerts

**MSI Afterburner** (https://www.msi.com/Landing/afterburner)
GPU monitoring and overclocking. Features: GPU temps, Fan curves, OSD overlay

steps.title: Cooling Optimization Tips
steps.content:
**Immediate Actions:**
• Use laptop on hard, flat surface (desk, cooling pad)
• Never use on bed, carpet, or soft surfaces
• Ensure all vents are unobstructed
• Keep ambient room temperature reasonable (below 30°C)

**Maintenance:**
• Clean vents with compressed air every 3-6 months
• Check for dust buildup in fan intakes
• Replace thermal paste every 2-3 years
• Consider professional cleaning annually

**Software Optimization:**
• Close unnecessary background applications
• Use Performance profile only when needed
• Limit FPS to your refresh rate (reduces heat)
• Undervolt CPU/GPU if comfortable (advanced)

steps.title: Undervolting (Advanced)
steps.content:
Undervolting can improve thermals but may cause instability if done incorrectly.

**Benefits:**
• Lower temperatures (5-15°C reduction)
• Reduced power consumption
• Less thermal throttling
• Quieter fan operation

**Tools:**
• Intel XTU - Official Intel undervolting tool (Intel CPUs)
• ThrottleStop - Popular third-party tool (Intel CPUs)
• Ryzen Controller - AMD CPU power management (AMD CPUs)

**Basic Steps:**
1. Download appropriate tool for your CPU
2. Start with small undervolt (-50mV)
3. Run stress test (Prime95, AIDA64)
4. If stable, increase undervolt by -10mV
5. Repeat until system becomes unstable
6. Back off to last stable voltage
7. Run extended stress tests (1+ hour)

infoBox.title: Caution
infoBox.content: Undervolting can cause system instability and crashes if done incorrectly. Always start with conservative values and test thoroughly.
